summary: This class models a thermostat: it stores one temperature reading and reports whether the system should be heating, cooling, or sitting idle. It is a small example of putting a decision rule inside a method so that the rule can be tested.

lines.text: The class is the blueprint for a thermostat object; each object made from it carries its own temperature reading.
The temperature is stored as a double so fractional degrees are allowed, and marking it private keeps outside code from changing it directly.
This constructor runs when a new Thermostat is created and demands a temperature, so no thermostat can exist without a reading.
The parameter and the field share a name, so `this.` is needed to say "the field belongs to this object" rather than reassigning the parameter.
All of the decision logic lives in one method that returns a String, which is exactly what makes it easy for a test to call it and check the answer.
Anything below 68 degrees is too cold, and returning immediately means the rest of the method is skipped.
This check is only reached when the temperature is 68 or above, so it correctly identifies the too-warm case.

Reaching this line means the temperature sits between the two limits, so the system does nothing; note that exactly 68.0 and exactly 75.0 land here, and those boundary values are the ones worth writing tests for.
